", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "Older notes"], "ref": "s130", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "85f52c31-27b5-4fe5-921a-ea411fb55932", "content": "## The image library and its metadata

Every approved image lives in the image library, and every image in it has a metadata record. Do not pick from the thumbnail grid and stop there. The thumbnail does not show you the limits on the image.

| Field | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| `id`, `filename` | Identity. Filenames were set by different people across several years and tell you little. |
| `type`, `title` | Rough category and a human label. |
| `description` | What is in the picture. Often thin, sometimes empty. |
| `tags` | Search help. Inconsistent, so never treat a missing tag as meaning anything. |
| `usage_rights` | The grant we hold for the file. |
| `restrictions` | The limits on this particular image. See below. |
| `added_date` | When it entered the library, which is not when it was made. |
| `source`, `attribution` | Where it came from. In-house work reads `internal-production`, and `attribution` is usually empty or names the in-house team. Empty attribution means no credit line is needed. |
| `width`, `height` | Pixel size. Check before you plan a crop. |
| `background` | How the image relates to what sits behind it. See below. |
| `safe_on` | Which grounds it can sit on. See below. |
| `variant_of` | Points at the parent when the image is one version of another. |

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "The image library and its metadata"], "ref": "s131", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "86969aea-4633-4607-bc0c-60994231516b", "content": "## 11. Governance

The folder contains documents from seven years, written by different people for different deadlines, and sometimes two of them disagree. This section says which one wins, who owns what, and how a piece of work gets approved. It takes precedence over any statement elsewhere about what is "final" or "current", including a file name.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "11. Governance"], "ref": "s132", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "86b7451f-baa7-4f78-b543-2cd8ad677052", "content": "### The values at work

| Value | What it looks like in marketing | What it rules out |
|---|---|---|
| Say what happened | A release note that names the bug | "Various improvements" |
| Contain first | The useful thing in the first line | A long wind-up about the threat landscape |
| Admit limits | A page that says which environments are unsupported | A feature table with a check in every box |
| Leave it better for the next on-call | A source file with a clear name and a note on why | A final deck that only one person can edit |

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "3. Values", "The values at work"], "ref": "s133", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "88232ed2-141f-4266-ba36-e451ef0a3866", "content": "### What fits and what doesn't

| Subject | Fits | Doesn't fit |
|---|---|---|
| A person at work | An engineer at a desk at dusk, reading a log | A team high-fiving around a laptop |
| Infrastructure | A real rack with labels and a worn floor | A computer-generated tunnel of light |
| The idea of containment | A single paper flame inside a paper ring | A digital barrier across a globe |
| AI agents | A simple cut-paper figure on a short lead | A glowing robot face |

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "9. Photography and illustration direction", "What fits and what doesn't"], "ref": "s134", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "8873c663-3967-4a15-92f2-c5e65fde3b3c", "content": "### Comparisons

"Faster than" needs a "than what". If the sentence compares to a named thing, that thing must be in the sentence. If it compares to a previous version of our own product, say which version.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "4. Numbers", "Comparisons"], "ref": "s135", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "8b8313bb-1412-4f76-8648-3f15a52d142a", "content": "### Exceptions

Exceptions are allowed and they are written down. Ask Noor by email with the piece, the rule, and the reason. If she agrees, the exception goes in the log she keeps, with an end date. Verbal approvals from a hallway don't count. Legal rules have no exception process through Brand. Those go to Priit.

Two exceptions from this year are typical. The Slow Burn Summit stage used a Soot and Ember backdrop well past the usual Ember proportion, because a stage is seen from 40 meters away. The Evenburn rename notice ran for 60 days using the previous product name in customer communications, so that people could find it.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "11. Governance", "Exceptions"], "ref": "s136", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "8cb0b048-4d9d-4fbb-aae3-79c022f6f5ad", "content": "## The hero

**A landing page hero shows product UI or a working room.** Those two options only.

That excludes illustration from the hero slot, even though we use it heavily elsewhere. Visitors on a landing page are deciding whether Wickhold is real. A screen from the product, or a real room where this work happens, answers that faster than a metaphor.

Use product UI when the page is about a product or a capability. Use a working room when the page speaks to a role or a problem and there is no single screen to show.

| Page | Hero |
|---|---|
| Quenchline product page | Product UI: one containment action |
| Evenburn product page | Product UI: exposure path or fix order |
| Leashgate early access page | Product UI: a tool-call policy, with the early access pill in frame |
| Platform engineering solutions page | Working room, or a terminal-adjacent product view |
| CISO or board-facing page | Working room. No people posing |
| Campaign page for the Containment Report | Working room |
| Event registration | A working session photographed at a past Slow Burn Summit, cleared for this use |

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "The hero"], "ref": "s137", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "8e229f98-1ea5-4a28-8b10-5f4b455449ff", "content": "## Email preheader

Every email has a preheader of at most 90 characters. It shows beside or under the subject line in most inboxes, so treat it as the second half of the subject. It must add something. Don't repeat the subject, and don't leave the field empty, or the client will fill it with the first text in the email, which for us is often the "view in browser" line.

Good: `Survey of 412 platform and security leaders on what happens after detection.`

Bad: `Containment Report 2026 is out. Read the Containment Report 2026 today.`

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "Email preheader"], "ref": "s138", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "92dc165a-1d79-4286-bdce-d5323f42f779", "content": "### Commissioning imagery

A good image brief names the idea, where the image will run and its one focal point, and it leaves the style to the visual guidance. "A wick in a ring of cut paper, for a blog on containment policy" is a usable brief. "Something cool about AI security" is not.

Freelancers and agencies should get the visual guidance before their first sketch. On the launch film, the first round of location photos came back blue and spotless, because the agency had worked from a mood board built on the old identity. Reshooting took a week.

Any generated or composited image gets the same review as a commissioned one. It is held to the same direction, and a person looks at it at full size before it goes anywhere.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "9. Photography and illustration direction", "Commissioning imagery"], "ref": "s139", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "930be8e8-ae39-4b4c-92f1-fb0b444f55be", "content": "## How the visual rules are layered

Three layers, read in this order.

1. **This page.** Applies to everything.
2. **The category.** What kind of image is it? Photo, illustration, icon, logo, product screenshot, chart, social graphic, event graphic, legal and trust imagery, anything showing a person.
3. **The content type.** Where is it going? Blog hero, LinkedIn, X, email header, landing page.

Most images touch one rule from each layer, and some touch two categories. A photo of a staff member at a customer site is photography and consent at once, and it has to pass both.

A lower layer can narrow a higher one. The illustration category accepts several formats, for example, and the blog hero page accepts fewer of them. In that case follow the narrower rule for that placement, and the broader rule stays true everywhere else. A lower layer cannot loosen this page. If a content-type page seems to let you do something this page forbids, bring it to Brand, because one of the two pages is wrong and we want to fix it.

Per-campaign exceptions go through Noor's exception log. Without an entry there, if a campaign needs something new, the rule changes for everybody or the campaign changes.

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "How the visual rules are layered"], "ref": "s140", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9444a373-5e1b-44c8-b229-396932ea45d4", "content": "## Body

Most of our email has three parts.

1. **What happened or what's new.** One or two sentences.
2. **Why it matters to this reader.** Two to four sentences. Different for a CISO list and a platform list, which is why the tracks are separate.
3. **What to do.** One button or link. Then the sign-off.

The working drafts are in the email templates, and the merge fields there match the sending platform. Start from a template. A blank page tends to produce an email that's 400 words long.

Good body copy, platform track:

> You downloaded the Containment Report, so here's the practical follow-up. Our rollout guide starts with Wickhold Quenchline in observe mode on one namespace, then moves to contain mode once you've read two to four weeks of would-have-acted events.
>
> It takes about an hour, and the failure modes are listed at the end.

Good body copy, CISO track:

> Decide whether your team tracks time to contain today. Your board will ask how long a runtime incident takes to contain. In our survey of 412 platform and security leaders, the median time to contain a runtime incident is 7.4 hours [Wickhold Containment Report, 2026, https://wickhold.example/containment-report].
>
> The report sets out how teams measure that number and what they report upward. If your team doesn't track it, section two is a place to start.

Bad body copy:

> Hope you're having a great week! As a valued member of our community, we wanted to reach out and share some exciting content we think you'll love. In today's rapidly evolving threat landscape, security has never been more important.

Four sentences in and the reader has learned nothing. Cut until the first sentence is the news.

Personalization: first name in the greeting when we have it, and role-based copy through segments. Anything else, like company size, industry or recent page views, stays out of the visible copy. Being told what you browsed by a security company is unsettling.

", "heading_path": ["Email playbook", "Body"], "ref": "s141", "relative_path": "brand/channels/email-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "94ad855d-2378-47b1-ba68-3bb6f5752827", "content": "## Withdrawal

A customer may withdraw at any time. Legal tells Noor, and owned assets are changed within five working days. Logo walls in decks are updated the same week. Events that have already printed are the only exception.
", "heading_path": ["Customer logo and quote policy", "Withdrawal"], "ref": "s142", "relative_path": "brand/legal/customer-logo-and-quote-policy.md"}, {"chunk_id": "95351c5f-43bc-488f-adc7-ddbebe98571a", "content": "# Wickhold voice and tone

Noor Eskelund, Head of Brand. Written for the February 2026 rebrand, rewritten in April after the Containment Report went out, last edited in June. Comments go to #brand-review in Slack.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone"], "ref": "s143", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "95a3bc17-3a62-42aa-bb1c-70545612062c", "content": "## 5. Code and commands

- Every code block must run. An engineer other than the author pastes it into a test cluster before publishing. Kofi keeps a throwaway cluster for this and will give you access.
- State versions at the top of the block or in the sentence before it: Kubernetes, Helm chart, kernel where it matters.
- Show the output when the output is the point, and trim it with a visible `...`.
- Use real-looking names like `payments-api` and `checkout`. Avoid `foo` and `my-app`, and don't use a customer's actual namespace names, even with permission.
- Say what fails. If `helm upgrade` can leave the agent in `CrashLoopBackOff` on an old kernel, put that in the post.

```bash
# Good: what you ran, and what to look for
kubectl get pods -n payments-api -o wide
# ...
# payments-api-6f9c7d   0/1   Terminating   0   3m   10.2.4.17   node-a
# A pod stuck here after a drain usually has a finalizer. Check that first.
```

", "heading_path": ["Writing for the Wickhold blog", "5. Code and commands"], "ref": "s144", "relative_path": "brand/channels/blog-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "96ddc51c-fae4-4130-b3cc-2deb903e70d4", "content": "# Word list

Everything here applies to anything a customer, prospect, journalist or candidate can read. Slack can say what it likes.

", "heading_path": ["Word list"], "ref": "s145", "relative_path": "brand/voice/word-list.md"}, {"chunk_id": "974c9dd1-f990-47ba-bc47-a49f901d010c", "content": "## Other rules for all images

**Current identity only.** Ember `#C2501F`, Soot `#15181C`, Tallow `#F4EFE6`, with Whetstone `#5E6B73` and Verdigris `#2F8F83` as secondary colors. Bricolage Grotesque, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono for any type on an image. Anything leaning on the 2024 blue palette or the 2024 logo is out, however good it looks. Some of those images are still in the library with no flag on them, so your eye is part of this check.

**No third-party marks.** No real product logos on laptop lids, no cloud provider marks on diagrams, no conference logos in a crop unless the agreement with that organizer allows it. Customer marks are a legal matter and go through Legal first.

**No watermarks,** no preview overlays, no leftover crop marks. If an image arrived with a watermark, its rights are not what you think they are.

**Do not stretch, tint or recolor library files.** Crop freely within the category's limits. Stretching breaks the proportions of the art and recoloring breaks the palette. Filters are out too: the warm look comes from the source image, and a filter laid on a cool image only makes it look cool and filtered. If an image needs a color change to fit, it is the wrong image.

**Export for the placement.** WebP or PNG for web, PNG where transparency matters, SVG for logos and icons when the placement accepts it. Keep web images under 400 KB unless the content-type page says otherwise. JPEG artifacts around Ember shapes are very visible, so check flat illustration at full size after compressing.

**Nothing that frightens.** Images follow the same stance as the copy. Show the small fire or the calm room, and skip the alarm. Red alert screens, countdown timers, sirens and skulls have no place here, even as a joke in an engineering post.

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "Other rules for all images"], "ref": "s146", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9792dec6-922e-42ef-aded-9a7b0bc70f03", "content": "## 2. The intro

A blog intro must cite a market statistic. Put it in the first two sentences, in the citation format from the style guide, and follow it with one sentence that says why this post exists. The rule is there because engineers are more willing to keep reading once they know the problem is measured and someone has measured it honestly.

Statistics are subject to the age limit in the approved claims, so check the date before you reuse an intro from an older post.

Market statistics are figures about the market or a surveyed population. Our own customer results and benchmark numbers belong further down the post, and they don't satisfy this requirement.

Good:

> The median time to contain a runtime incident is 7.4 hours [Wickhold Containment Report, 2026, https://wickhold.example/containment-report]. Most of the teams we talk to can tell you how long detection took. Far fewer can tell you what happened in the hours after. This post is about those hours.

Good:

> 41% of platform teams need more than six hours to contain a runtime incident [Wickhold Containment Report, 2026, https://wickhold.example/containment-report]. A lot of that time goes to one question: who is allowed to touch the workload? Here is how to settle that question before the page goes off.

Bad, because it has no statistic and no reason to read on:

> Kubernetes has changed how modern teams ship software, and with that change come new security challenges.

Bad, because a customer result is doing the job of a market statistic:

> Lowmoor Credit Union cut time to contain from 4 hours to 11 minutes. Here's how your team can get the same results.

", "heading_path": ["Writing for the Wickhold blog", "2. The intro"], "ref": "s147", "relative_path": "brand/channels/blog-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "98588c52-bb4f-4b97-8b2e-da0afede6983", "content": "## 15. Usage notes

- **a/an:** go by sound. An eBPF agent, a SOC 2 report, an SRE.
- **back end** (noun), **back-end** (adjective).
- **cyber:** avoid as a prefix. Say what kind of security you mean.
- **data** is singular in our copy: "the data is".
- **drain:** a verb in Kubernetes and in our copy. "Drained the node."
- **e.g., i.e., etc.:** write "for example", "that is", or finish the list.
- **email:** no hyphen.
- **failover** (noun), **fail over** (verb).
- **in order to:** "to".
- **log in** (verb), **login** (noun). Same pattern for **set up / setup**, **roll out / rollout**, **shut down / shutdown**.
- **real time** (noun), **real-time** (adjective).
- **sidecar, service mesh:** lowercase, one and two words.
- **startup:** one word.
- **third party** (noun), **third-party** (adjective).
- **trade-off:** hyphenated.
- **utilize:** "use".
- **very, really, extremely:** delete and reread.
- **via:** "through", unless it's a technical path.
- **zero-day:** hyphenated, and only for an actual zero-day.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "15. Usage notes"], "ref": "s148", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "99b64151-dd64-4f1d-afb3-b4f3e8dbee05", "content": "## FAQ

Pull questions from sales calls, not from what we wish people asked. Answer in two sentences or fewer. A good FAQ answers the objection that would otherwise stop the form.

> **Will this take down production?**
> In observe mode, Wickhold Quenchline takes no action. You choose when and where contain mode starts.

> **How much overhead does the agent add?**
> Under 2% CPU overhead on a typical node in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "FAQ"], "ref": "s149", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9b333c21-ba1c-413a-bd7a-144ac492a1b9", "content": "### The brand idea

A wick is where a fire is allowed to exist. It gives the flame a place to be, and it keeps the flame there. That is the idea behind the name, the mark and the tagline. Wickhold accepts that production systems have heat in them. The job is to hold it to a small, known place.

This idea should explain design and copy decisions when a rule doesn't. When two options are both on brand, pick the one that feels calmer and more contained.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "4. Positioning", "The brand idea"], "ref": "s150", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9d594429-aec3-41bb-bf14-e0c498d102f8", "content": "### Owners

Read it out loud as a handover to the next on-call. If you stumble, or feel you are selling to a colleague, rewrite that part.

Then a few checks that catch most problems:

- Can a stranger tell what happened, what is contained and what is next?
- Does each claim have a figure and a source, or is it a plain description of what the product does?
- Is there an "I" or "we think" outside a signed founder piece?
- Does anything rely on the reader being scared?
- What's the last line doing there?

Copy review goes through #brand-review, and Noor or one of the brand team turns it around in two working days. Claims go to Priit Salonen's team and take the time the approved claims set. If a deadline leans on either of those, say so early.
", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone", "Before you send it for review"], "ref": "s152", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9eeb0cca-0fab-4d0b-aba9-a395e700120f", "content": "# Blog hero images

Content team working rules, June 2026.

**Every blog post has one hero. It is a 16:9 illustration or photo. It is never a dashboard.**

Product UI in the hero looks like an ad on top of an article, and the detail goes illegible at the size most people see it, which is the preview card. If a post is about a product screen, put the screenshot in the body, at a size where it can be read.

", "heading_path": ["Blog hero images"], "ref": "s153", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/blog-hero.md"}, {"chunk_id": "9fa331ad-cbeb-4c25-ab4f-ffc8fb3d18ec", "content": "### Choosing between them

| If the piece is about | Lean toward |
|---|---|
| People, customers, the company | Photography |
| An idea or a risk | Illustration |
| What the product does | Product imagery |

Security imagery has a set of tired visual habits, and the brand stays well clear of them. Fear is not part of the visual language, for the same reason it is not part of the verbal one.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "9. Photography and illustration direction", "Choosing between them"], "ref": "s154", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "a1cb5f0e-a0a0-4e46-9bcf-3ae99202023b", "content": "## Hero copy

The hero says what the product does and who it's for, in that order. Lead with what happens to the reader's workload. Our tagline can sit in the hero of the brand page, but it doesn't describe a product, so product pages shouldn't rely on it.

Good, product page:

> **Contain runtime failures before they spread**
> Wickhold Quenchline detects bad behavior in Kubernetes and isolates a pod, freezes a process or drains a node, under the policy you set.
> [Book a demo]

Good, posture page:

> **Know which misconfiguration to fix first**
> Wickhold Evenburn tracks drift across cloud and cluster, finds each exposure path and gives your team a fix order.
> [See a sample report]

Good, early access page:

> **Set policy for what AI agents can call**
> Wickhold Leashgate, in early access, applies tool-call policy at runtime and limits what a compromised agent can do.
> [Request early access]

Good, report page:

> **The Wickhold Containment Report 2026**
> A survey of 412 platform and security leaders on how long containment takes, and where the hours go.
> [Read the report]

Good, brand page:

> **Small fires stay small.**
> Wickhold is the runtime security company for teams that run Kubernetes.
> [See how it works]

Bad, from a 2025 agency concept:

> **Next-level cloud security for the modern enterprise**
> One powerful platform. Total confidence. Peace of mind at every layer of your stack.

Nothing in that hero says what the software does. It would fit a mattress company if you swapped "stack" for "bed".

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Hero copy"], "ref": "s155", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "a46a0775-894e-42be-977d-0610b7c892ae", "content": "## Deliverability

A security vendor's mail gets scanned hard, and a lot of it lands in quarantine. Keep the sending domain authenticated, and check with IT before anyone adds a new sending tool. Avoid link shorteners. Don't attach files. Link to the page instead, as PDFs from vendors are often stripped at the gateway. Contacts with no opens in a year go to the re-engagement note, and if they don't respond, off the list.

", "heading_path": ["Email playbook", "Deliverability"], "ref": "s156", "relative_path": "brand/channels/email-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "a55aa74f-5cd7-4ad5-b930-7c95b442740a", "content": "## Old pages

Any page without traffic for six months gets redirected. Campaign pages get an end date at launch. In the 2026 rebrand cleanup, the web team found pages from 2023 still live and indexed, which is how you end up with a stale claim ranking above the current one. Put the end date in the brief.
", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Old pages"], "ref": "s157", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "a5eca255-6e97-40a8-be37-f50288aba296", "content": "### Money

- Dollars with the symbol: $18, $29. No ".00".
- Node pricing is written in full: "$18 per node per month". Not "/node/mo", not "per-node", not "$18 pnpm", which someone did actually write in a deck.
- Funding and other large sums use a capital M and no space: $46M. Don't write "$46 million" in one place and "$46M" in another; pick the M.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "4. Numbers", "Money"], "ref": "s158", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "aaf2972c-7d1e-457d-8af8-632e772bef8b", "content": "### Company

The legal name is Wickhold, Inc., which appears in legal notices, contracts and the copyright line. The brand name is Wickhold, pronounced WICK-hold. "Wickhold Security" is the former brand name, and it survives only in historical references such as a press archive.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "5. Brand architecture", "Company"], "ref": "s159", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "abdccafa-35be-4ed9-a7fc-57720e907977", "content": "## T8b. Field Day follow-up

Owner: the Field Day host. Plain text, within two days of the event.

**Subject:** What we showed at Field Day {{city}}
**Preheader:** The commands from the live session, and the answer to the question we ran out of time on.

Hi {{first_name}},

Thanks for coming on {{date}}. The commands from the live session are on the page below, with the seeded incident if you want to run it yourself.

We ran out of time on {{open_question}}. {{short_answer}}

**[See the session notes]**

{{host_first_name}}, Wickhold

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "T8b. Field Day follow-up"], "ref": "s160", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "abf52a1c-e75d-4337-8a09-6ceaa48a588c", "content": "## Reuse across pages

A/B test variants use the same hero rule. If you test a hero, both arms must pass. An illustration "just for the test" still fails, and test pages have a way of becoming permanent.

Do not use the same working-room photo on two product pages. Visitors move between them, and a repeated picture makes the site look small.

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "Reuse across pages"], "ref": "s161", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "abfc6c9b-fa74-4690-92be-fe600f22909f", "content": "### Translation

Legal wording is not translated freely. If an asset is localized, the translated version of the approved GDPR sentence comes to me first, and a claim that was fine in English does not stay fine because a translator softened or sharpened it.

", "heading_path": ["Regional rules: EU and UK copy", "Translation"], "ref": "s162", "relative_path": "brand/legal/regional-rules-eu-uk.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ac2ef319-64a9-42c8-b403-4fe159097fc2", "content": "## Timing

Tuesday to Thursday, 9 to 11am in the recipient's time zone where the platform knows it. Customer notices go when they're ready, at any hour. Avoid the last week of a quarter for prospect sends, because sales wants clean inboxes for their own outreach, and avoid the week of the big cloud-native conference in November unless the send is about the conference.

If a customer notice is going out, hold marketing sends to the affected accounts for 48 hours. Nobody wants a newsletter in the same hour as a CVE note. Lifecycle owns the pause, and the on-call engineer writing the notice tells them in the channel.

", "heading_path": ["Email playbook", "Timing"], "ref": "s163", "relative_path": "brand/channels/email-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b0b53749-5be6-4308-8b5a-8b34e65f5020", "content": "## 10. Tried and dropped

Guest posts from partners took more editing than writing one ourselves, and the partners wanted a link in every paragraph. Weekly "news roundups" lasted nine weeks in 2025 and nobody missed them. Keyword-led briefs from an agency produced the "Everything You Need To Know" titles above, and we stopped that contract in the spring.
", "heading_path": ["Writing for the Wickhold blog", "10. Tried and dropped"], "ref": "s164", "relative_path": "brand/channels/blog-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b1963df5-8f44-4062-a767-6c822e7f71e4", "content": "### Regulators and public bodies

Do not name a regulator, or imply that a regulator has reviewed Wickhold. Do not use a guidance document as a sales hook while it is in consultation.

", "heading_path": ["Regional rules: EU and UK copy", "Regulators and public bodies"], "ref": "s165", "relative_path": "brand/legal/regional-rules-eu-uk.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b2af5123-9ec1-4562-8c1d-22ea9532be1c", "content": "### The three families

| Family | Role | Why it was chosen |
|---|---|---|
| Bricolage Grotesque | Headlines | Slightly irregular, with some personality at large sizes. It looks made by a person |
| IBM Plex Sans | Body | Plain and sturdy, and easy to read over long documents |
| IBM Plex Mono | Code | Pairs with Plex Sans and has clear distinctions between similar characters such as 0 and O |

All three are open-licensed, so anyone at the company, any agency and any build pipeline can use them without a license request. Inter was retired with the 2024 identity.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "8. Typography", "The three families"], "ref": "s166", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b39ffdf9-91aa-4c47-a19d-da6e58b90e6e", "content": "## 12. Social and email formatting

- No emoji in brand posts or email. Founders can do as they like on their own accounts within reason.
- One link per post. Put it where it reads naturally; shortened links are for tracking and shouldn't appear as bare text where the full domain would fit.
- Line breaks on LinkedIn mark real paragraph breaks. No one-sentence-per-line posts.
- Greeting in email: "Hi Sam," with the first name and a comma, or no greeting for a broadcast. No "Dear". No "Hey there".
- Plain sign-off: name, job, company, or the team name on a broadcast. Nobody signs "Cheers" on a customer notice.
- In email, check that the piece reads correctly with images off.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "12. Social and email formatting"], "ref": "s167", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b7195205-6479-423b-bbc7-d14ba956b98e", "content": "## What didn't work

- Fortnightly newsletter. Unsubscribes rose and we had nothing to say on the off weeks.
- "Webinar replay" emails after every webinar. Replaced by one line in the newsletter.
- A six-email welcome series. Most people stopped opening at the third. Now three emails.
", "heading_path": ["Email playbook", "What didn't work"], "ref": "s168", "relative_path": "brand/channels/email-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "b7b87728-b779-4387-aded-a12e59f856d7", "content": "## 1. Headlines

**Headlines are in sentence case.** Capitalize the first word and any proper noun. Everything else is lowercase.

This covers page titles, blog titles, section headings, email subject lines, slide titles, buttons, nav labels, form labels, table headers and any text set over an image. If it looks like a heading, it is one.

| Right | Wrong |
|---|---|
| What contain mode does to a running pod | What Contain Mode Does To A Running Pod |
| Wickhold Containment Report 2026 | WICKHOLD CONTAINMENT REPORT 2026 |
| How Ostler Grocers cut its open critical misconfigurations | How Ostler Grocers Cut Its Open Critical Misconfigurations |

Details:

- Product names, event names and the report title keep their capitals, as do Kubernetes, Helm, CVE and the rest of the proper vocabulary. `containerd` and `eBPF` keep their lowercase starts even as the first word, though it's nicer to rewrite so that neither opens a headline.
- The word after a colon is lowercase: "Drift: what it is and how to read it".
- No full stop on headlines. The tagline is the one exception, and it keeps its full stop everywhere.
- No code formatting in headlines. They break in email clients and in link previews.
- Keep a headline to one idea. If it needs a colon and a dash, it's two headlines.

The old sheet used Title Case for everything over 24px. That went in the rebrand, and pages still carrying it get fixed when someone next touches them.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "1. Headlines"], "ref": "s169", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ba11321a-3c46-44c9-b56c-ba0b84503c24", "content": "### Writing the company name

Write Wickhold, with one capital. The possessive is Wickhold's. The name is singular in American English, so "Wickhold is", and it never takes "the" in front of it. In a logo-free context such as a plain-text email or a form field, the name is simply typed out. Internal team names like "Wickhold Marketing" are descriptions and do not need any special treatment.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "5. Brand architecture", "Writing the company name"], "ref": "s170", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "bab04564-38bc-4e96-ba78-9bb00fa98da6", "content": "### Email and event lists

- Do not import badge scans or partner lists into a send until field marketing confirms the lawful basis for that list.
- Every EU and UK send carries an unsubscribe link and the Wickhold, Inc. postal address.
- Bought lists are not used in these regions. This was tried once in 2025 for a German webinar and dropped after the complaints.
- Event pages say who receives attendee data before the attendee registers.

", "heading_path": ["Regional rules: EU and UK copy", "Email and event lists"], "ref": "s171", "relative_path": "brand/legal/regional-rules-eu-uk.md"}, {"chunk_id": "bc78b090-211c-4c83-92b8-ef866c9adc03", "content": "### Say the number, then stop

Claims carry a figure and a source. No adjective stacks.

"Fast" is not a claim. "A fast, powerful, highly scalable runtime platform" is three non-claims in a row. Write the number, say where it came from, and end the sentence. The urge to add a second sentence explaining why the number is impressive is the urge to resist. A reader who needs that sentence is the wrong reader; a reader who doesn't will think less of us for it.

Bad: "Lowmoor Credit Union saw an incredible, game-changing reduction in response times."

Good: "Lowmoor Credit Union cut time to contain from 4 hours to 11 minutes across 220 nodes."

Bad: "Quenchline is extremely lightweight and blazingly quick."

Good: "Wickhold Quenchline contains a known-bad process in a median of 38 seconds in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026."

If there is no figure, there is usually no claim, and the honest move is to describe what the product does in plain mechanical terms. "Isolates a pod's network" needs no number and no source. It's a description. "Industry-leading isolation" needs both and has neither.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone", "What Wickhold believes", "Say the number, then stop"], "ref": "s172", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "bd7ba1fe-13b7-4692-afd2-ef01d0dc122b", "content": "## Review

Check the last ten posts on the blog before you commit. The same image twice in a month makes the blog look thin, and readers on the index page see them side by side. Since a hero image goes out in the social card by default, check the record's `restrictions` as you would for social use.

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "T1. Report announcement"], "ref": "s177", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c0c60096-8668-4c20-87fe-10c000e9f1d1", "content": "## By email type

| Email | Header |
|---|---|
| Monthly newsletter | One hero illustration crop, changed each issue |
| Report announcement | Illustration taken from the report cover art, with its title removed |
| Event invitation | Photo crop or illustration, cleared for event use |
| Product update | Usually none. A small product crop in the body does more |
| Sales follow-up | None |
| Renewal or billing notice | None |

Do not animate headers. Some mail apps only show the first frame, which then has to work alone. Do not slice a header into several image cells. That technique causes hairline gaps in the same older apps that dislike large images.

Keep one crop per campaign and reuse it across the sequence, so that the second and third sends read as a set. Each one still gets its image record checked, because `restrictions` can change between sends.

", "heading_path": ["Email header images", "By email type"], "ref": "s178", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/email-header.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c1079d42-ff19-496b-9bbf-e72c382dc03d", "content": "## Page skeleton and word budget

| Section | Budget (words) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hero: headline, one sentence, CTA | 40 | Must make sense with no scrolling |
| Proof strip: customer logos or one number | 25 | One row, no carousel |
| What it does: three blocks at most | 150 | Concrete actions, not themes |
| How it works or how you roll it out | 100 | Steps. Commands if the audience is technical |
| Customer proof: one result, one quote | 70 | A full sentence with the number and the source |
| FAQ: three questions at most | 80 | Real questions from sales calls |
| Closing CTA | 15 | Same action as the hero |
| **Total** | **480** | Leaves 20 words of slack |

CTAs follow the shared CTA format in the email templates. Use one primary CTA per page, repeated at the top and bottom with the same wording. A secondary link is allowed for a technical reader who is not ready for a form, like the docs or the rollout guide.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Page skeleton and word budget"], "ref": "s179", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c1483026-3308-4a52-8cf9-e6314d11b35f", "content": "## 6. Grammar and punctuation

- **American spelling** in all copy, including copy going to UK and EU readers. Containerize, not containerise.
- **Oxford comma**, always. It has settled more than one argument in Kubernetes prose, where lists of nouns can double as lists of objects.
- **Active voice** with a named actor, wherever the actor is known. "Wickhold Quenchline drained the node." If the passive is hiding who did it and that person is us, it goes.
- **Tense.** Past for what happened, present for what the product does, and nothing in the future except where a date is public.
- **Contractions** are fine in the blog, on social and in email. Skip them on legal pages and in anything aimed at a board.
- **Colons** are our favorite punctuation mark and they're doing fine. Use them to introduce the fact.
- **Semicolons** at most once a page. If there are two, one wants to be a full stop.
- **Em dashes** rarely in body copy. Most are a full stop that lost its nerve. Spaced en dashes are not a substitute.
- **Parentheses** for the short aside only. If the aside matters, promote it to a sentence.
- **Quotation marks:** double, with commas and full stops inside, American style, except for literal strings in technical writing where the punctuation would change the meaning. Single quotes only inside double.
- **Italics:** titles of reports and the occasional stress only. They disappear on Soot grounds and in email.
- **Bold:** for scanning in long documents, once or twice per section. Bold on a landing page means the design isn't working.
- **Ampersands:** only in proper names. Plain "and" in headlines too.
- **"And/or"** is a legal term. Pick one.
- **Slashes** as a shortcut ("platform/security teams") get rewritten: "platform and security teams".

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "6. Grammar and punctuation"], "ref": "s180", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c1865b41-5cea-419f-8a42-5a9096193a21", "content": "### Positioning statement

For teams that run Kubernetes in production, Wickhold is the runtime security company that contains failures early. Other tools report what they saw. Wickhold products act on it, within limits the customer's team has set, and tell the team what was done.

This statement is internal. It tells writers where the company stands, and it is not customer copy. The approved public description of the company is the current boilerplate, which is kept and owned separately.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "4. Positioning", "Positioning statement"], "ref": "s181", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c28e7438-46d7-471e-b55d-ea5418751c6c", "content": "## Document posts and video

PDF document posts are off the plan, for the same reasons as carousels. Native video follows the screenshot rules for captures. A title frame counts as an image and falls under the seven-word cap.

", "heading_path": ["LinkedIn images", "Document posts and video"], "ref": "s182", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/linkedin-image.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c37df191-6216-45a0-a492-50686e14a2e5", "content": "### One focal point

Every image has one focal point. A reader should be able to say what the image is of after a second's look. If two things compete, crop or pick another image.

Tests we use in review:

- Squint at it. One shape or area should hold.
- Shrink it to a thumbnail. Something should still be identifiable.
- Describe it in one short sentence without "and". "An engineer reading a terminal in a dark room" passes. "A team at a table and a wall of monitors and a logo on the door" does not.

Collages, split screens and before-and-after pairs fail this unless they are charts, where the comparison is the single point.

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "The two rules that come up every week", "One focal point"], "ref": "s183", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c555aa43-f86c-4b00-af8f-ab621338c84f", "content": "## 4. Certification status

SOC 2 Type II: held. Renewed January 2026. The report is shared under NDA through the account team.

FedRAMP Moderate: in process. The approved sentence is "Wickhold is pursuing FedRAMP Moderate authorization." Never state or imply FedRAMP authorization or certification. The status sheet has the detail and is the first thing to check.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "4. Certification status"], "ref": "s184", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c6a52d68-5c35-45b0-aceb-b1a1e1b7e799", "content": "## 17. Accepted shortcuts and exceptions

- Internal documents (including this one) don't need to meet the citation form. They do need to be right.
- Slide speaker notes follow the same rules once they go into a shared deck, since decks get forwarded.
- Quoted customer language stays as approved, including its capitalization. If a quote has a problem, go back to the customer through the customer marketing owner; don't fix it in place.
- Text inside a screenshot is not edited. If a screenshot shows something out of date, take a new one.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "17. Accepted shortcuts and exceptions"], "ref": "s185", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c7346580-863d-4b26-aa24-4419525276a3", "content": "## T4. Field Day invite

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "T4. Field Day invite"], "ref": "s186", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "c954e1a8-3bea-4b8c-9f2e-9284e8e1cfd0", "content": "## Proof

Each number sits with its source in the same block, so nobody has to scroll to a footnote to check it. These are approved as written:

- Lowmoor Credit Union, 220 nodes: time to contain fell from 4 hours to 11 minutes.
- Ostler Grocers, 1,900 nodes: 63% fewer open critical misconfigurations in 90 days.
- Under 2% CPU overhead on a typical node in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026.

Don't round them, combine them or place two customers' numbers in one sentence. One page gets one customer story. Stacking every number we have makes the page feel like a pitch deck, and readers trust a single detailed result more.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Proof"], "ref": "s187", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ca1ba113-65da-4917-9655-fa55f8b6ad6f", "content": "## Reading old copy

Pre-2026 material is everywhere: the archive, old decks, the sales team's memory. It sounds different for a reason. The old brand sold watching. It leaned on "always", "every" and "complete", and it got excited in public. A lot of it is competent copy for a company we no longer are.

If you are reusing something from before the rebrand, do not patch the sentences. Take the facts, check that they are still approved, and write it again. Look for these symptoms when reading a draft that someone has recycled: a promise of total coverage, a sentence about seeing with nothing about what happens next, and an excited tone that doesn't match the numbers beside it.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone", "Reading old copy"], "ref": "s188", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ca3468d9-9da9-4734-a3d6-9c0497716473", "content": "## 5. Statistics: 12-month age limit

A market statistic may not be older than 12 months at publication. This is the limit on how old a statistic can be, and it is measured on the day the piece goes out, not the day it was drafted. A post queued in March for release in May is checked against May.

The limit applies to market and survey statistics only. It covers any figure that describes the industry, the market, or a population of teams. It does not apply to customer results such as the Lowmoor and Ostler outcomes, or to product metrics such as the lab figures, which have their own qualifier.

The age of a statistic runs from the publication date of its source. Fieldwork dates do not matter. A report re-quoted in a newer article keeps its original date, so a 2026 article quoting a 2024 survey is a 2024 statistic.

Applied to our own reports:

| Source | Published | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Wickhold Containment Report 2026 | April 14, 2026 | Usable for publication through April 14, 2027 |
| Wickhold Field Report 2024 | 2024 | Past the 12 months limit |
| Wickhold Field Report 2023 | 2023 | Past the 12 months limit |

The two Containment Report statistics in section 1 are the only market statistics of ours inside the limit today. The Field Report figures still appear in old decks and old posts. That is an archive problem and not a permission. Do not reuse them. Do not reword them to make them feel new, and do not refer to them as "historically" true.

Fresh third-party statistics are allowed without coming to me first, with the source link and the date of the source in the copy. The source must be a named publisher and the figure must appear on the page you link to. A figure found in a vendor's blog, quoting another vendor's blog, gets traced to the original or is dropped. The third party's name still has to clear the competitor rules.

When the 2027 Containment Report is published, section 1 will be updated and the 2026 figures remain usable until they reach the limit. Old assets stay in the archive as they are. They are not re-promoted once a market statistic in them has expired. Paid and email reuse counts as publication.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "5. Statistics: 12-month age limit"], "ref": "s189", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ca490efc-da47-4269-b919-e60bd97f97e1", "content": "## Regional rules: EU and UK copy

Priit Salonen, with notes from the field marketing review, August 2026

Applies to anything aimed at readers in the EU or the UK: campaigns, event pages, email sends, localized landing pages, press outreach, partner co-marketing. If a global asset will run in those regions, it is regional copy too.

", "heading_path": ["Regional rules: EU and UK copy"], "ref": "s190", "relative_path": "brand/legal/regional-rules-eu-uk.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ca65b949-2e3b-43fc-b1a9-0f6770fb82d8", "content": "## CTA format for all channels

This lives here because the email team wrote it down first, and it now applies to every channel: email, landing pages, paid, social, the blog, event pages.

A CTA, the call to action on a button or a link, is at most four words, and it starts with a verb. The same CTA wording rules apply wherever the button sits. "Learn more" and "Click here" are banned everywhere, including as link text inside a sentence.

| Fine | Not fine |
|---|---|
| Read the report | Learn more |
| Book a demo | Click here |
| See the rollout guide | Click here to see the rollout guide |
| Request early access | Early access request |
| Save your seat | Your seat is waiting for you |

Say what happens on the other side of the click. "Get started" is allowed but weak, so use something more specific if you can.

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "CTA format for all channels"], "ref": "s191", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ca8bf1aa-ced7-4c7e-871d-281a24c0f561", "content": "## 10. Links

Link text names the thing the reader will get: "the 2026 Containment Report", "the Helm values reference". The surrounding sentence should still read correctly if the link is dead. Don't link a whole sentence. Internal pages open in the same tab.

UTM parameters come from the campaign tracker, not from memory. Marketing ops reject hand-typed ones.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "10. Links"], "ref": "s192", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cb464fca-10ce-4726-92c8-69e56971c97d", "content": "## Not cleared

**Vaskell Health is not cleared.** Do not use the name, logo, people, quotes or results in anything external, and do not use them in a customer-facing deck. "A large health system" does not help, because the draft material is specific enough to identify them. The draft case study in the folder stays a draft. No approval was given, and a finished-looking layout does not change that.

Everyone else is not cleared by default. Companies seen in a contract, in a support ticket, or in a Slow Burn Summit attendee list are not references.

", "heading_path": ["Customer logo and quote policy", "Not cleared"], "ref": "s193", "relative_path": "brand/legal/customer-logo-and-quote-policy.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cb9cd1ab-7cf6-4dd3-84c9-391e53813754", "content": "## The character

Wickhold is someone who has been paged more often than you have and is not going to bring it up.

**Unhurried.** Nothing in our copy is urgent. A page that hurries the reader is using the same trick as the alert fatigue they came to us to get away from.

**Exact.** "Isolated the pod's network" beats "took action". "220 nodes" beats "at scale". If two engineers would argue over what a sentence means, it isn't finished.

**Unimpressed by itself.** The product is useful. Copy that gasps at it reads as though the writer has not seen it fail. We have seen it fail, and the release notes say so.

**On your side of the pager.** The reader is a peer on the same rota, and we write to them as someone who could take the next shift. No lecturing, no "did you know", no explaining Kubernetes to people who run it.

When the character slips, it usually slips into one of four people:

- **The hero.** Rushes in, saves the day, gets the credit. Early rebrand drafts leaned on firefighters and helmets until Maren pointed out that a firefighter arriving means it already went badly. The customer's on-call team is the competent party in every story we tell.
- **The prophet.** Sees doom everywhere and sells shelter from it. The whole security industry's default register, which makes it invisible to the people we want to reach.
- **The buddy.** "Hey there, Kubernetes friends." Nobody paged at 3am wants a pal.
- **The analyst.** "In today's rapidly evolving threat landscape." Sentences with no one in them. If nothing would change when the paragraph is deleted, delete it.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone", "The character"], "ref": "s194", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cd94a510-5949-4cb4-ae6a-bba3ddd34472", "content": "### Raising a conflict

If two documents disagree, don't quietly pick one and move on, because the next person will hit the same thing. Follow the order of authority for the piece in hand, ship it, and then send a short note to the owner of the lower document.

A useful note says three things and takes a minute to write:

> "These two documents give different answers on the same point. I used the higher one. Can the other be updated?"

The owner corrects the lower document or explains why it stands. If the higher document is the one that's out of date, the owner of that document changes it. Nobody overrides it locally.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "11. Governance", "Raising a conflict"], "ref": "s195", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cd981fdd-c863-4776-8686-3ab4cc8e9dc8", "content": "## 8. Spoken claims, demos and records

Spoken claims count. A webinar is a publication, a sales call can end up quoted in a procurement file, and a recorded conference talk stays available for years. Speakers get the same tables as writers. Questions from the floor that go beyond them are answered with "I will get back to you", and then with an email to me.

Demo environments show synthetic data. A demo may show a containment action in contain mode, and the timing shown on screen is not a claim about customer environments. Presenters should say so if anyone asks. Screenshots from a real customer tenant are not used in any circumstance.

The owner of each asset keeps the published version, or a link to it, and the source for each figure in it for three years. When a claim is withdrawn I will send a list of the assets I know about. I do not know about all of them, so owners should search their own material.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "8. Spoken claims, demos and records"], "ref": "s196", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cde0d081-7f1e-4ee9-a5cb-3a4e3d01ea38", "content": "## 9. Updating old posts

Older posts stay up, but they can mislead. The brand team runs through the top 30 posts by traffic every quarter. Each gets one of three outcomes: leave it, edit it in place with an "Updated" date at the top, or redirect it to a newer post.

Edit in place when a product name, a command or a figure has gone out of date. Redirect when the advice has changed. Never quietly change a claim. If a post said something that turned out to be wrong, add a line saying what changed and when. Engineers notice, and they remember how you handled it.

", "heading_path": ["Writing for the Wickhold blog", "9. Updating old posts"], "ref": "s197", "relative_path": "brand/channels/blog-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "ced40b51-cf38-4400-ba4a-10544d338867", "content": "### Product imagery

Screenshots and diagrams show the real product and real terms. When a choice exists between a clever visual metaphor and a clear view of what the product did, show the product.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "9. Photography and illustration direction", "Product imagery"], "ref": "s198", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cefc4366-9544-4ad9-930d-06a08e27c623", "content": "### Percentages

**Percentages use digits and the % symbol.** Always, including at the start of a sentence, in headlines, in legal-reviewed copy and in speech written for a stage.

- Right: 41% of platform teams, 63% fewer open critical misconfigurations.
- Wrong: forty-one percent, 41 percent, 41 per cent, 63pc.

No space before the symbol. "Percentage points" is written out when you mean the difference between two percentages, and it's rare enough in our copy that a reviewer will ask if you're sure.

", "heading_path": ["Content style guide", "4. Numbers", "Percentages"], "ref": "s199", "relative_path": "brand/style/content-style-guide.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cf9f8743-ae58-4da5-89b8-03e46292615a", "content": "## Spec

**600px wide. No text in the image.**

The file itself is 600px wide. We tried a 1200px source scaled down in the HTML, and a couple of older desktop mail apps rendered it at full width and broke the layout. So: exactly 600, height between 150 and 240, under 150 KB.

No text means none, and it is stricter than other placements that allow overlay set in design. A large share of readers load email with images off, and headers get blocked first. If the headline is in the picture, those readers get an empty box. Headlines, dates and CTAs go in live HTML. A header image that says "Slow Burn Summit" in type is out, even when a designer set it properly and even if the art is otherwise approved. Put the event name in the first line of the HTML.

That also rules out the social templates, which all carry type, and charts, which need labels.

", "heading_path": ["Email header images", "Spec"], "ref": "s200", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/email-header.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cfd8736c-24f6-4637-a4fe-87e329a80ab5", "content": "### Wickhold Leashgate (early access)

Leashgate is in early access. Claims describe what the early access product does today. They do not describe a roadmap, and they do not give a date.

Permitted vocabulary is tool-call policy, agent identity, and the blast radius of an agent. The approved outcome statement is "limits what a compromised agent can do".

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "2. Claims that need a qualifier", "Wickhold Leashgate (early access)"], "ref": "s201", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "cff1ee61-653f-40b6-b141-8a57f205945f", "content": "### Market statistics

Name the source and the year each time. A market statistic in a headline needs its source on the same screen or page section. See section 5 for how long a statistic stays usable.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "2. Claims that need a qualifier", "Market statistics"], "ref": "s202", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d0c14399-2877-40a1-b9e2-08aa9c6cf979", "content": "## Anonymous examples

An unnamed customer story needs the same evidence as a named one and Legal's review of the wording. Keep the sector broad and leave out numbers that could be traced. Do not invent a composite customer.

", "heading_path": ["Customer logo and quote policy", "Anonymous examples"], "ref": "s203", "relative_path": "brand/legal/customer-logo-and-quote-policy.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d1e89004-baf1-4226-8278-0203deb6a9f7", "content": "### Why the company rebranded

The 2024 brand made a promise about watching. It suited a company that sold visibility, and it stopped fitting as the product moved on. By 2025 the feature customers talked about in renewals was the moment Wickhold Quenchline isolated a pod's network at 3am and nobody had to get out of bed. Sales calls kept going the same way: the prospect would say every tool they owned could see a problem, and then ask what happens next.

Ilse Varga-Holm, who owns the rebrand, started the work in spring 2025 with a set of about 30 customer and on-call interviews. Maren Tolliver and Dov Achterberg sat in on most of them. The clearest finding was that nobody wanted another thing watching them. They wanted the blast of an incident to be smaller and the morning after to be shorter. That finding drove every decision below.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "1. What changed in 2026", "Why the company rebranded"], "ref": "s204", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d3a7bb51-c97b-4e21-b17b-38dcc852c60b", "content": "## Transparency and dark mode

Do not use transparent PNGs in email headers. Spot illustrations and other `background: transparent` files are out here, whatever their `safe_on` says. Several mail apps darken the message in dark mode, and they do it unevenly: some swap the ground and leave images alone, and some invert parts of both. A flat ground inside the image keeps the header predictable. Always send a `solid` or `scene` image.

The wordmark sits in its own table cell above the header image, as a panel variant, with alt text. Do not bake the logo into the header picture, since the header is blocked more often than a small logo and you lose the sender's identity with it.

", "heading_path": ["Email header images", "Transparency and dark mode"], "ref": "s205", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/email-header.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d3e16b9a-7001-4119-b693-e318a563bf94", "content": "## Lists and segments

| Segment | Who | Tone in one line | Usual sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform | Platform engineers, SREs, DevSecOps | Practical, can carry code | Newsletter, platform nurture, product announcements |
| Security leadership | CISOs, security directors | Short and plain | CISO nurture, report, Summit invite |
| Customers, technical | Named admins and on-call contacts | Facts and steps | Product announcements, customer notices |
| Customers, executive | Sponsors on the account | Short, rarely | Founder notes, Summit invite |
| Event-local | Contacts within driving distance of a Field Day | Friendly, practical | Field Day invite and reminder |

Role tags come from enrichment and are wrong about one time in ten. If a reply says "I'm not a CISO", fix the contact on the day. Never merge the platform and security leadership lists to reach a volume target. We did that for the 2025 report and the CISO list's unsubscribe rate doubled in a single send.

", "heading_path": ["Email playbook", "Lists and segments"], "ref": "s206", "relative_path": "brand/channels/email-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d46b6260-77fa-4102-a897-17a53c50ada1", "content": "### Mistakes seen since launch

The single most common mistake since launch is treating Ember as the "main" color because the table calls it primary. Primary means most important, and it does not mean most area.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "7. Color", "Mistakes seen since launch"], "ref": "s207", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d4925866-8875-4cbd-9a6f-d1368287a31e", "content": "## Size and crop

Export at 1600x900. Most library heroes and photos are 3:2, so you will lose some height. Crop from the top and bottom, then check that the focal point has survived. A hero illustration's focal element usually sits off center and the quiet part can go. Some platforms crop preview cards further, so keep the focal point out of the outer tenth of the frame.

Do not upscale. A 1536-wide source enlarged to 1600 is about the limit, and it should look clean at full size.

", "heading_path": ["Blog hero images", "Size and crop"], "ref": "s208", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/blog-hero.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d5917474-5628-4710-bcee-8fc4d508b8f4", "content": "### Lab figures

Two product figures come from Wickhold's own lab. Both must carry the phrase "in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026", in the same sentence as the figure.

| Figure | Required form |
|---|---|
| CPU overhead | "under 2% CPU overhead on a typical node in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026" |
| Containment speed | "contains a known-bad process in a median of 38 seconds in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026" |

A footnote does not meet this requirement. An asterisk does not meet it. A qualifier on the slide before does not meet it. In a chart, the phrase goes in the chart title or directly under it. In a talk, the speaker says it aloud.

The figures describe a lab, so they may not be presented as field results or customer averages. "Known-bad process" is part of the claim: it does not extend to unknown processes, novel techniques, or "threats" in general. Reports may repeat the figures only if the benchmark year stays attached. When the 2027 benchmarks run, the year changes and this table is reissued. Nobody edits the year by hand.

Approved:

> Wickhold Quenchline adds under 2% CPU overhead on a typical node in Wickhold lab benchmarks, 2026.

Not approved:

> Quenchline contains attacks in 38 seconds.

> Under 2% overhead. Guaranteed.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "2. Claims that need a qualifier", "Lab figures"], "ref": "s209", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d5f392ba-4c2a-4e26-a0e3-ce5038a40e1f", "content": "## Legal pages carry no people

Terms, privacy, subprocessors, the DPA page, and the like: no people in any image on these pages. That covers portraits, illustrated silhouettes, hands in a shot and a team in the footer strip. The same applies to the legal section of any combined page.

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "Legal pages carry no people"], "ref": "s210", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d62a25c1-8dcf-4f5f-9fca-e5ace68eb593", "content": "### Change log

Allowed: a silent loop of a containment action, under ten seconds, with a poster frame that passes the hero rule by itself. Not allowed: a talking-head brand film. We tried one on the old homepage and the bounce numbers were bad enough to end the debate.

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "Video in a hero"], "ref": "s212", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d7e32a81-295b-4582-b2b6-886d3e810933", "content": "## How-it-works blocks

This is where the two audiences differ most. For engineers, show the thing itself. A short command block costs few words and earns more trust than a paragraph:

> **Install in observe mode**
> `helm install quenchline wickhold/quenchline --set agent.mode=observe`
> The agent attaches to each node. Nothing is contained until you change the mode.

For security leaders, give steps in terms of time and ownership:

> **Week one:** Quenchline runs in observe mode on one cluster.
> **Weeks two to four:** Your team reviews what it would have done.
> **After week four:** You decide which namespaces move to contain mode.

Both describe the same rollout. Neither should use a diagram that needs a paragraph to explain it.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "How-it-works blocks"], "ref": "s213", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d885263f-9b82-40d8-9414-559f313ac4d9", "content": "## Further down the page

Sections below the hero have more room. Spot illustrations work in feature rows. Check each section's ground, since landing pages usually alternate Tallow and Soot bands, and a `safe_on: light` file dropped in a Soot band disappears. Nav and footer logos need checking band by band as well.

Screenshots in the body can run larger and carry callouts. Keep one image per section at most.

Customer logo strips: only what Legal has approved, and no more than the approved set, even when a strip looks empty. Keep them in one tone. Do not recolor logos in Ember.

Quote portraits go through the people and consent check first.

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "Further down the page"], "ref": "s214", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d97e9a51-4ed8-4abd-8345-0e8776039628", "content": "## Build and review

1. Brief, with Noor's OK on audience and goal.
2. Copy in a shared doc with a word count at the top. Over 500 goes back.
3. Claims check by Priit, with sources pasted next to each claim.
4. Design and build. Web team needs five business days for a new layout and two for an existing one.
5. Staging review on a phone first. Most paid traffic arrives there.
6. Launch, then a check at two weeks: is anyone completing the form, and where do they drop off?

Use the existing layouts when you can. We have three (product, campaign and report) and each has been tested for load speed and for the mobile form. A page built from scratch needs a reason, and "it's a special campaign" isn't one.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Build and review"], "ref": "s215", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d97fd5bf-b314-4163-8e1f-2521813ecbb0", "content": "## Timing against the event calendar

Dated images age badly. A card that names a date comes down from the scheduled queue the moment the date moves. After the event, do not reuse it. Set `restrictions` on the record when you file it, as with any time-limited card.

", "heading_path": ["LinkedIn images", "Timing against the event calendar"], "ref": "s216", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/linkedin-image.md"}, {"chunk_id": "d9f2e784-f2b4-4f9e-b5e6-d57329727181", "content": "## Pricing on pages

Product pages link to the pricing page and don't repeat its contents. Tiers change, and the pages that repeat them never get updated. Paid-search pages for pricing queries can show a short tier summary pulled from the pricing page, reviewed by Priit before launch.

", "heading_path": ["Landing pages", "Pricing on pages"], "ref": "s217", "relative_path": "brand/channels/landing-page-playbook.md"}, {"chunk_id": "da7fb90d-c48a-4764-8849-02eabfb2f1c3", "content": "### What moved

Hero image under 250 KB on the wire. Serve WebP with sizes set, and do not lazy-load the hero. SVG for logos and icons. Everything below the fold lazy-loads. A slow page is a credibility problem for a company that sells to platform engineers, and they will open dev tools.

", "heading_path": ["Landing page imagery", "Performance"], "ref": "s219", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/by-content-type/landing-page-imagery.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dbe61209-03fd-4a5d-bbbc-40c4921862dc", "content": "### Containment is the whole argument

Something will get through. Every serious engineer already knows this, and the companies who claim otherwise are talking to someone else. Wickhold's position is that the useful question is how far a failure gets and how fast it stops spreading. The whole product line follows from that, and so does most of our vocabulary. If a draft reads as though nothing bad will ever happen to the customer, it's arguing for a different company.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold voice and tone", "What Wickhold believes", "Containment is the whole argument"], "ref": "s220", "relative_path": "brand/voice/voice-and-tone-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dbeda12a-d4c4-456b-98a4-03870d27d7a5", "content": "## T8d. Deprecation notice

Owner: product. At least 60 days ahead of the change.

**Subject:** {{feature}} ends on {{date}}
**Preheader:** What's changing, who is affected and how to move before then.

Hi {{first_name}},

On {{date}} we're removing {{feature}} from {{product}}.

**Who is affected.** Clusters running {{condition}}.

**What to do.** {{numbered_steps}}

**What happens if you don't.** {{plain_failure_mode}}

Reply to this email if the date doesn't work for your change window, and we'll talk.

**[Read the migration guide]**

The Wickhold team

", "heading_path": ["Email templates", "T8d. Deprecation notice"], "ref": "s221", "relative_path": "brand/templates/email-templates.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dc3bc010-0485-41ce-88ec-cb162a2de295", "content": "### No generated text in any image

No image contains text produced by an image model or baked into artwork by a tool that does not treat it as live type. Models misspell product names, invent letterforms and produce near-English that survives one quick look and then gets screenshotted by a customer. We had a test hero in spring where a wall sign read almost like "Quenchline". Nobody caught it until it was in a review deck.

Text in a Wickhold image is set by a person, in the design tool, in the brand typefaces, as a separate layer over finished art. That covers overlays, labels, chart annotations and callouts.

Three things do not count as generated text:

- Words that are really in the scene: a printed rack label, a whiteboard someone wrote on, a door sign. Check that they say nothing embarrassing and name nobody outside the company.
- Real interface text in a true product screenshot.
- The wordmark, which is a vector file, placed by a person.

Some placements allow no overlay at all and others cap it. The content-type page has the number.

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "The two rules that come up every week", "No generated text in any image"], "ref": "s222", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dc77a88e-0005-4ab3-bbd6-129c941f008e", "content": "### Tagline

The current tagline is **Small fires stay small.**

It is written with sentence case and a full stop, and the full stop is part of it. Do not vary it, translate it into a campaign pun, or extend it with a second clause. It can stand alone under the logo, close a piece, or sit at the end of a deck. It does not need to appear in every piece, and one use per piece is the limit.

The retired 2024 tagline should not appear in anything new, including "then and now" pieces, without a request to Brand.

", "heading_path": ["Wickhold brand guidelines 2026", "4. Positioning", "Tagline"], "ref": "s223", "relative_path": "brand/guidelines/Brand_Guidelines_2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dce37ce3-fd82-47df-a26e-44c4f3ee9a0e", "content": "## Asking for something new

If the library has nothing suitable, do not borrow from the web, do not pull an image from a past deck, and do not take it from a teammate's desktop. Files outside the library have no record and nobody can check their rights.

Requests go to the brand designers through the design queue with the placement, the deadline and one sentence on what the image should show. Allow five working days for illustration and more for photography that needs a shoot. Anything made for you gets a metadata record before it ships.

", "heading_path": ["Visual rules common to every image", "Asking for something new"], "ref": "s224", "relative_path": "brand/visuals/00-visual-rules-common.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dd77c0c2-9cd8-4804-84c6-5405807045df", "content": "### Customer count

The only approved claim is "more than 140 customers". The following are not approved: "140+ customers", "nearly 150 customers", "hundreds of customers", "thousands of engineers", or any count of nodes, clusters or workloads summed across the customer base. Finance reconciles the number each quarter against active contracts. Pilots, lapsed accounts, open-source users, and companies that attended Slow Burn Summit are not customers for this purpose.

When the reconciled number supports a higher claim, this document will change. Until it does, the number in a sales deck, a conference bio or a partner page is the number here. If you have seen a larger figure in circulation, it is wrong, and I would like to know where you saw it.

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "1. Claims approved as written", "Customer count"], "ref": "s225", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "dde20031-29bf-4c0b-91c9-c5d802e24e23", "content": "## 2. Claims that need a qualifier

", "heading_path": ["Approved claims, 2026", "2. Claims that need a qualifier"], "ref": "s226", "relative_path": "brand/legal/approved-claims-2026.md"}, {"chunk_id": "df7a48a0-30d0-48b6-a58b-e765719e808b", "content": "### What Wickhold is and is not

| A runtime security company | A general cloud security suite |
| Focused on Kubernetes | Trying to cover every kind of infrastructure |
